subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Social Learning in Markets
description: A fast breakdown of Social Learning in Markets for builders.

hook.text: A new restaurant opens. The first few diners love it and tell friends. A cascade starts and the place is booked.

buildup.text: Social learning means updating beliefs based on others' actions, not just your own information. We use others as data.

discovery.text: Banerjee and Bikhchandani showed cascades form when people ignore private signals and follow observed behavior instead.

twist.text: Cascades are fragile. One piece of public contradictory information can collapse the entire chain overnight.

climax.text: Social learning is useful but brittle. When everyone copies, one mistake propagates through the network instantly.

punchline.text: Learning from others works until everyone is learning from each other.

quiz.question: What makes informational cascades fragile?
options: Too many participants make them stronger
One public contradictory signal can collapse the entire chain
Cascades are self-reinforcing and never break

details.summary: Social learning occurs when people use others' observable choices as information about product quality, investment value, or market conditions. This rational observational strategy can create information cascades where everyone follows early movers regardless of private information.
details.whyItMatters: Social learning explains herd behavior in financial markets, viral product adoption, and restaurant popularity. When people rationally ignore private information in favor of observed behavior, markets can converge on wrong choices collectively.
takeaways: Observing others' choices provides useful information about quality
Information cascades occur when social signals override private knowledge
Herding behavior can lead markets to incorrect collective conclusions

faq.question: What is an information cascade?
faq.answer: When early adopters choose a product, later observers rationally infer it must be good and follow suit regardless of their own information. Each follower reinforces the signal for the next. The cascade can persist even if the initial choice was wrong.

faq.question: How do information cascades affect stock markets?
faq.answer: Investors observe that others are buying a stock and infer those buyers have positive information. This drives more buying independent of fundamentals. The resulting bubble persists until enough contrarian information breaks the cascade.
